children: could have another lever to extend Azure growth even after its recent acceleration, with BNP Paribas arguing that higher pricing may gradually boost cloud revenue as customer contracts renew. The firm also sees a possible SpaceX
cloud-computing deal as a future catalyst, giving investors two additional ways Microsoft could strengthen an already powerful AI infrastructure story.
BNP Paribas analyst Stefan Slowinski said Microsoft executives acknowledged that Azure pricing is moving higher, but existing contracts will not be rewritten.

Instead, pricing will be reset upon renewal, suggesting any Azure pricing benefit should feather into results gradually rather than create a material step-up in Azure growth over the near-term, Slowinski wrote.

That distinction matters because Microsoft said Azure's recent acceleration into the mid-40% growth range has not been driven materially by pricing. Instead, fleet-level efficiency improvements and continued capacity additions remain the main contributors.
For investors, that leaves pricing as a potential incremental tailwind rather than something already embedded in recent growth.
Slowinski maintains a Buy rating and $549 price target on Microsoft.

The analyst also highlighted Microsoft's continuing need for more computing capacity. Executives pushed back somewhat on reports that the company plans to expand data-center capacity to 38 gigawatts by 2032, but reiterated that Microsoft remains in catch-up mode and is continually searching for additional compute.
That is where SpaceX could enter the picture.

Microsoft declined to confirm any relationship, but Slowinski said we would not be surprised if there is a potential future announcement. SpaceX recently disclosed a new compute customer expected to spend roughly $1 billion per month starting in December, adding intrigue around Microsoft's possible involvement.

The bigger near-term signal is Azure pricing. Investors should watch renewal cycles, cloud growth and whether higher prices begin adding to revenue without hurting demand. A confirmed SpaceX deal would provide another capacity source, but execution and economics would matter more than the headline. Microsoft also said OpenAI revenue sharing is not currently driving Azure's outperformance, reinforcing that core cloud demand remains the central piece of the thesis.

title: BNP Paribas Spots What Could Move Microsoft Stock Next
